# CSCI 435 PR review

You are drafting a code review that the user (GitHub login `ab-wm`) will test, edit and post on a
teammate's PR in `CSCI-435-SE/gitea`, a course fork of Gitea. The review is a graded course
deliverable, so the user stays its author: you gather the facts, check them, and hand back a
draft in their format. Don't post, approve or comment on the PR, and don't push to it. Don't offer
to fix the author's code either. In this course the author makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

The user's standing instruction for reviews is "not *that* deep". That doesn't mean overlooking
real problems, and it doesn't mean nitpicking every small one. The code is not going upstream. A
finding belongs in the draft only if it would change a score, or if the author would want to know
about it before merging.

## 1. Find your footing

Work out where you are running, because that decides how you fetch the PR and where the draft goes.

- **Claude Code inside the repo clone** (`gh` works, and the working tree is the fork). Use `gh`
  for PR data and read source files locally. The user is usually on their own feature branch, so
  don't switch it. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>` and read files
  with `git show pr-<N>:<path>`. Compare with `git diff origin/main...pr-<N>`, because local
  `main` is often behind.
- **Chat, or anywhere without the clone.** The repo is public. Use a GitHub connector if one is
  attached. Otherwise fetch the URLs in `references/fetching-without-the-repo.md`. If nothing can
  reach GitHub, ask the user for the PR link and the diff.

## 2. Triage

First get the PR's title, author, changed files and linked issue (`Closes #N`). Then decide how
much review it needs. The user only does a full review when code changed:

- **The PR is already merged, or the user has already reviewed it.** Say so first, quoting their
  existing review in a line. Continue only if they want a fresh look, for example a re-review
  after new commits. Don't let their earlier scores steer yours.
- **The PR only touches check-ins, docs, course files, showcase material, AI logs, or config like
  `.coderabbit.yaml`.** Skip the rubric. Skim the files for anything surprising, such as code
  hiding in a "docs" PR, a secret, or a file in the wrong folder. Then suggest a one-line
  approval in the user's voice, for example "All good, just the check-in doc and AI log. No need
  for complete review."
- **The PR is the user's own.** Nobody approves their own PR in this course. Say so, and offer a
  list of findings instead of a rubric.
- **This is a follow-up after the user asked for changes.** Check only the items they asked for.
  If those are done, suggest a short approval such as "All good now!"
- **The PR changes code or tests.** Do the full review described below.

## 3. Gather, lightly

Read these in order, and stop once you can score every rubric row:

1. The PR description, and the linked issue's acceptance criteria (ACs) and design decisions.
   The rubric is scored against the ACs.
2. The diff. Skip `ai-logs/**`: those files are thousands of lines of chat transcript, and they
   are not reviewed.
3. CodeRabbit's comments and the author's replies, so you don't repeat what was already raised
   and fixed.
4. The CI status, if you can see it.
5. Just enough of the code the diff touches or depends on to check its claims. In the clone,
   `.claude-students/INDEX.md` lists short docs for each area if you need background.

Don't run lint, builds, servers or e2e suites unless the user asks. CI already runs lint and the
tests, and the user does their own hands-on testing. Don't split the review across subagents.

Aim for about 10–15 tool calls on a typical PR. In testing, runs that went to 35 calls produced
no better drafts than shorter ones would have. Spend those calls on checking the findings that
will go in the draft, one check each. Don't chase ideas you won't include. Don't read the
author's AI logs, and only download a library's source when a finding depends on it. If you go
over the budget, write the draft with what you have, and say what you didn't check.

## 4. What to check

- **Each AC.** Find where it is implemented and where it is tested. A missing AC is the main
  reason to lower the Correctness score.
- **Whether the tests can fail.** A test that would still pass with the feature removed doesn't
  count as coverage. Look for:
  - assertions that read a value without first asserting it exists;
  - `test.fail()` or skips that cover more than the one known failure;
  - checks that only test whether something is present.
- **Course rules that graders look at:**
  - a `## Tech Debt` section;
  - an AI assistance section;
  - before/after screenshots when templates, CSS or Vue files change;
  - Conventional Commit messages that end in `(#N)`;
  - `Assisted-by` trailers, and no `Co-Authored-By`;
  - commits small enough to review, for example split by layer.

  If you are unsure of the current sprint's rules, read `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, or
  fetch it.
- **Claims in the PR description.** Descriptions are often drafted by AI. Check one or two
  concrete claims against the code, such as a timing, a count, or "every test does X".

Check every finding against the source before it goes in the draft. Reviews of AI-written code
tend to produce confident findings that turn out wrong. A wrong finding in a posted review costs
the user more than a missed nit. If checking disproves your idea, drop the finding or reword it.
For example, on #105 a suspected "silent pass" turned out to fail loudly, so the finding became
about the unhelpful error message instead.

Leave out style nits, anything lint or CI catches, CodeRabbit findings the author already fixed
(credit those in one line), and anything that wouldn't change a score.

## 5. Scoring

Start every row at 10, and deduct points only for a concrete gap you can name. Past reviews show
how the user scores:

- A UI change without before/after screenshots: Documentation 8, Overall 9, "Yes, once the
  screenshots are added".
- One large commit instead of commits split by layer: AI transparency 7.
- A factual error in the description or the Tech Debt section: Documentation 8.
- Everything checks out: 10s, and Overall 10, "Yes".

A deduction needs a *required* point behind it, something you would ask the author to change before
merging. An observation you'd only file under "Strictly optional" (one AC covered by unit tests but not
end to end, a small AI-assisted commit the description doesn't mention) leaves the score at 10. The user
has scored a feature PR 10 on every row even though optional observations like these existed.

Overall is "Yes" unless something required is missing. Nits don't block a merge. Any score below
7 needs a note saying what would raise it, because the course rubric requires one.

## 6. Draft format

Use the rows from the course rubric. Read `.github/code-review-rubric.md` from the repo, or from
raw GitHub, so the draft picks up any change to the rubric. The template below matches the rubric
as of Sprint 2.

Write in the user's voice:

- short, plain sentences;
- one sentence per table note;
- no rule citations in the table;
- `file:line` for code findings.

Skim one of the reviews in `references/posted-examples.md` before you draft. These are reviews
the user actually posted.

```markdown
### Code Review — @ab-wm

TODO (you): what you ran, clicked or checked yourself.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |

### Strictly optional for completeness
**<the point in a few words>.** <one or two sentences, with file:line>

### AI-Log
Review was drafted by AI, and then changed to better fit the review structure and my inspection of the files. Log available on #<linked issue>.
```

- **Required changes** go in the note of the row they affect, written as a request ("please add
  before/after screenshots, as they are required"). Overall then says "Yes, once X is added".
- **Optional points** go in their own section after the table. Keep at most one or two, and drop
  the section if there are none.
- **The testing line** stays a visible `TODO`. It records what the user checked by hand, and they
  write it themselves. Don't fill it with what you did. A visible placeholder can't be posted by
  accident without being noticed.

## 7. Hand it back

- **In Claude Code**, write the draft to `.specstory/pr-<N>-review.md` (the folder is
  gitignored). If that file already exists, it may be the user's edited copy, so write the draft
  to `pr-<N>-review-2.md` (or the next free number) instead.
- **In chat**, give the draft as one fenced markdown block, so the table copies cleanly.

Then write a short summary in chat, about 10–15 lines:

- the verdict;
- each finding, marked required or optional;
- what you checked and what you didn't (for example, "didn't run the e2e suite"), so the user
  can write their testing line;
- any idea you couldn't verify, offered as something the user could try in their own testing.
  Unverified ideas never go in the draft.

End there. Remind the user to file this session's AI log as `ai-logs/README.md` describes, since
the AI-Log section points to it.

TITLE: fix(UI): label picker aria expanded (#104)
AUTHOR: Jack-Donohue
MERGEABLE: MERGEABLE

BODY:
Closes #104

## What changed
The Fomantic ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts` now wraps each dropdown module's own `hide` method. After the original `hide` runs, the wrapper schedules the existing `refreshAriaActiveItem` 100 ms later. That is the same delay the `blur` listener uses for the hide animation. The e2e test that recorded the bug no longer carries `test.fail()`.

## Why
The label picker in the issue sidebar kept `aria-expanded="true"` after Escape closed its list, so a screen reader announced it as expanded. Only the `focus`, `blur`, `mouseup` and arrow-key `keyup` listeners refreshed the attribute. When Escape closes the list, focus stays on the picker, so none of them run.

The issue first proposed wrapping the `onHide` setting. The sidebar pickers set their own `onHide` after the patch runs (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:231-236`), and Fomantic merges new settings over old ones, so that wrapper would have been replaced. Wrapping the module method avoids that, because Escape (`dropdown.js:1649-1651`) and `dropdown('hide')` both go through it. The picker's own `onHide`, which saves the labels, still runs inside the original `hide`.

This fixes the Expected Behavior in #104: `aria-expanded` becomes `false` when Escape closes the list.

## How it was tested / Test strategy
- **Unit (Vitest), new:** two tests in `dropdown.test.ts`, under "expanded state on hide". They build a combobox dropdown that sets its own `onHide` after init, as the label picker does. One closes it with Escape and the other with `dropdown('hide')`. Each checks that `aria-expanded` is `"false"` 100 ms later, and the Escape test checks that the picker's `onHide` ran exactly once. Both failed before the fix (`expected 'true' to be 'false'`) and pass after it.
  - The test dropdown has a hidden input in place of the picker's search box. happy-dom moves focus into a search box when the list opens, and blurring that box on hide would trigger the old `blur` refresh and hide the bug. In the browser, focus stays on the picker, which the e2e test checks.
- **E2E (Playwright), changed:** removed `test.fail()` from `issue label picker reports collapsed after Escape` in `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts`. It now passes in a real browser on the real issue page. The existing `issue labels can be selected and deselected by keyboard` test presses Escape and checks the label is saved, so it covers the risk named in the issue's Consequences.

Unit tests come first because the cause sits in one module that can be tested without a server. The e2e test confirms the real picker, whose focus behaviour happy-dom doesn't reproduce.

## CI / manual verification
- `pnpm exec vitest`: 63 files, 375 tests passed
- `make lint-js`: passed
- `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts' make test-e2e`: 12 passed in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including the Escape test without `test.fail()`, and the keyboard label-save test
- CI: <status once the PR runs>

## Design
Follows the revised Decision 1 in #104 (wrap the module's `hide`, not the `onHide` setting), confirmed after the spec review.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The fix replaces a Fomantic internal method (`module.hide`) rather than using a public callback. A Fomantic upgrade that renames or restructures `hide` would silently undo it. The unit tests would catch that. The existing `set.direction` patch in the same function carries the same risk.

**Encountered:** `dropdown.ts` keeps `aria-expanded` up to date by re-reading the menu's classes from timers scheduled by several DOM listeners, rather than from Fomantic's show/hide lifecycle. That is why this hide path was missed. I added the missing path and didn't restructure the rest, since #25 may move the label picker off Fomantic (see the note in `multiselect-aria.test.ts`). The file's own TODO, that multiple selection is only partly supported, still stands.

I checked the Fomantic call paths it cited, ran the unit, lint and e2e checks, and can explain each change. AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.

TITLE: Label picker keeps aria-expanded="true" after Escape closes it
AUTHOR: controlled-opposition

## Observed Behavior
Escape closes the label picker's list in the issue sidebar, but the picker keeps `aria-expanded="true"`. A screen reader announces the picker as expanded while its list is closed.

The picker is a Fomantic dropdown with `role="combobox"`. Gitea's ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts` sets its `aria-expanded`.

## Expected Behavior
`aria-expanded` changes to `false` when Escape closes the list, as it does when the picker loses focus.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Sign in, and open an issue in a repository that has at least one label.
2. Press Tab until the **Labels** picker in the sidebar has focus. The list opens.
3. Wait at least 150 ms.
4. Press Escape.
5. Inspect the picker. The list is hidden, focus is still on the picker, and `aria-expanded` is `"true"`.

If you press Escape less than 100 ms after the picker gets focus, `aria-expanded` changes to `"false"`. Step 3 avoids that case.

## Additional Information
- Found on commit `4f8e6ec205` in Chromium and WebKit, through Playwright on macOS.
- Cause, from reading the code: `refreshAriaActiveItem` in `dropdown.ts` sets `aria-expanded`. Only the `focus`, `blur` and `mouseup` listeners and the arrow-key `keyup` listener call it. No listener calls it when Escape closes the list.
- Focusing the picker also fires a `blur` listener, which schedules `refreshAriaActiveItem` 100 ms later. An Escape inside those 100 ms is corrected by that refresh. This hides the bug from a test that presses Escape immediately.
- The test `issue label picker reports collapsed after Escape` in `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts` records this bug. It is marked `test.fail()` and links to this issue. When the bug is fixed, the test passes, and Playwright reports it as a failure. Remove the `test.fail()` line in the same PR as the fix.
- Found by #65.

## Design Decision
### Decision 1: refresh the ARIA state when the dropdown module hides
**Decision:** In `delegateDropdownModule` in `dropdown.ts`, wrap the Fomantic dropdown module's own `hide` method. The wrapper calls the original `hide` with the same arguments, then calls `deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100)`. The 100 ms delay matches the `blur` listener, which waits for the hide animation. Confirmed by the implementer, @Jack-Donohue.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Wrap Fomantic's `onHide` setting, the way the function wraps `onLabelCreate`. This was the first proposal. A later `dropdown('setting', {onHide})` call replaces the wrapper, because Fomantic merges new settings over old ones (`dropdown.js:3732-3736`). The label picker makes that call (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:231-236`), and so do the `.jump` dropdowns (`common-page.ts:73-81`). The fix would miss the exact picker this issue is about.
- (b) Add Escape to the `keyup` listener that refreshes the state on arrow keys.
- (c) Watch the menu's `class` attribute with a `MutationObserver`, and refresh the state on every change.

**Rationale:** Escape and every other internal close call `module.hide()` (`dropdown.js:1649-1651`). Calls such as `$dropdown.dropdown('hide')` also go through the same module object, so one wrapper catches every hide. It isn't a setting, so later `setting` calls can't replace it, and `dropdown.ts:133-147` already patches the module the same way for `set.direction`. Option (b) is smaller but fixes only Escape. Option (c) catches every hide, but it runs on every animation class change and adds an observer to every dropdown on the page.

**Consequences:** `module.hide()` still calls `settings.onHide` itself, so the label picker's save (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:209-211`) runs unchanged. The existing e2e test `issue labels can be selected and deselected by keyboard` checks this, since it presses Escape and checks the saved list. The patch depends on a Fomantic internal method name, the same risk the `set.direction` patch already carries. A Fomantic upgrade must recheck both. The fix PR adds a Vitest case in `dropdown.test.ts` and removes the `test.fail()` line from `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts`.


## Scope
small

[Jack-Donohue]
Spec reviewed — the steps reproduce and the cause is right, but Decision 1 has to change before I implement it.

1. **Blocking:** the `onHide` wrapper never runs for the label picker. `delegateDropdownModule` wraps `onHide` on the first `.dropdown()` call. After that, `IssueSidebarComboList.init` calls `dropdown('setting', {…, onHide})` (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:231-236`). Fomantic's `setting` does `$.extend(true, settings, name)` (`web_src/fomantic/build/components/dropdown.js:3732-3736`), which replaces the wrapper with the picker's own `onHide`. The `.jump` dropdowns in `common-page.ts:73-81` would lose it the same way. I'd wrap the module's `hide` method instead, the way `dropdown.ts:133-147` already wraps `set.direction`. Escape calls `module.hide()` (`dropdown.js:1649-1651`), and `module.hide()` still calls `settings.onHide` (`:553`), so the picker keeps saving labels. Later `setting` calls can't undo this wrapper. I'd keep the `onHide` wrap as a rejected alternative, with this reason.
2. Consequences asks for a new test that checks the label is saved. One already exists: `issue labels can be selected and deselected by keyboard` presses Escape and checks the sidebar list (`multiselect-aria.test.ts:52-53`). I'd name it there instead.
3. `dropdown.test.ts` already loads the real Fomantic build, so a Vitest case is possible. It would set `onHide` through `setting` after init, then show, hide and check `aria-expanded`. That covers the fix and point 1 without a browser. AGENTS.md prefers unit tests.

// Fomantic marks the chosen items of a multiple selection dropdown "active"
function refreshAriaSelected(dropdown: HTMLElement) {
  if (!dropdown.classList.contains('multiple')) return;
  for (const item of dropdown.querySelectorAll(':scope > .menu > .item')) {
    item.setAttribute('aria-selected', item.classList.contains('active') ? 'true' : 'false');
  }
}

function onDropdownAfterFiltered(this: any) {
  const $dropdown = $(this).closest('.ui.dropdown'); // "this" can be the "ui dropdown" or "<select>"
  const hideEmptyDividers = $dropdown.dropdown('setting', 'hideDividers') === 'empty';
  const itemsMenu = $dropdown[0].querySelector('.scrolling.menu') || $dropdown[0].querySelector('.menu');
  if (hideEmptyDividers && itemsMenu) hideScopedEmptyDividers(itemsMenu);
}

// delegate the dropdown's template functions and callback functions to add aria attributes.
function delegateDropdownModule($dropdown: any) {
  const dropdownCall = fomanticDropdownFn.bind($dropdown);

  // the "template" functions are used for dynamic creation (eg: AJAX)
  const dropdownTemplates = {...dropdownCall('setting', 'templates'), t: performance.now()};
  const dropdownTemplatesMenuOld = dropdownTemplates.menu;
  dropdownTemplates.menu = function(response: any, fields: any, preserveHTML: any, className: Record<string, string>) {
    // when the dropdown menu items are loaded from AJAX requests, the items are created dynamically
    const menuItems = dropdownTemplatesMenuOld(response, fields, preserveHTML, className);
    const div = document.createElement('div');
    div.innerHTML = menuItems;
    const $wrapper = $(div);
    const $items = $wrapper.find('> .item');
    $items.each((_, item) => updateMenuItem($dropdown[0], item));
    $dropdown[0][ariaPatchKey].deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem();
    setTimeout(() => refreshAriaSelected($dropdown[0]), 0);
    return $wrapper.html();
  };
  dropdownCall('setting', 'templates', dropdownTemplates);

  // the `onLabelCreate` is used to add necessary aria attributes for dynamically created selection labels
  const dropdownOnLabelCreateOld = dropdownCall('setting', 'onLabelCreate');
  dropdownCall('setting', 'onLabelCreate', function(this: any, value: any, text: string) {
    const $label = dropdownOnLabelCreateOld.call(this, value, text);
    updateSelectionLabel($label[0]);
    return $label;
  });

  // Fomantic doesn't call onAdd/onRemove on the initial load, so pre-selected items stay silent
  for (const [callbackName, selected] of [['onAdd', true], ['onRemove', false]] as const) {
    const callbackOld = dropdownCall('setting', callbackName);
    dropdownCall('setting', callbackName, function(this: any, value: string, text: string, $item: any) {
      const ret = callbackOld.call(this, value, text, $item);
      if ($dropdown[0].classList.contains('multiple')) {
        // a value typed by the user and removed by its label has no menu item
        $item?.[0]?.setAttribute('aria-selected', selected ? 'true' : 'false'); // the changed item is exact now, before Fomantic updates its classes
        announceSelectionChange($item?.[0]?.textContent.trim() || value, selected);
        setTimeout(() => refreshAriaSelected($dropdown[0]), 0); // Fomantic updates the "active" classes after the callback
      }
      return ret;
    });
  }

  // Escape and `dropdown('hide')` both run the module's hide, but no listener sees them when the focus stays put.
  // wrap the method, not the onHide setting: callers like the issue sidebar pickers set their own onHide later, replacing a wrapper.
  const oldHide = dropdownCall('internal', 'hide');
  dropdownCall('internal', 'hide', function(this: any, ...args: any[]) {
    const ret = oldHide.apply(this, args);
    $dropdown[0][ariaPatchKey].deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100); // the same delay as the blur listener, for the hide animation
    return ret;
  });

  const oldSet = dropdownCall('internal', 'set');
  const oldSetDirection = oldSet.direction;
  oldSet.direction = function($menu: any) {
    oldSetDirection.call(this, $menu);
    const classNames = dropdownCall('setting', 'className');
    $menu = $menu || $dropdown.find('> .menu');
    const elMenu = $menu[0];
    // detect whether the menu is outside the viewport, and adjust the position
    // there is a bug in fomantic's builtin `direction` function, in some cases (when the menu width is only a little larger) it wrongly opens the menu at right and triggers the scrollbar.
    elMenu.classList.add(classNames.loading);
    if (elMenu.getBoundingClientRect().right > document.documentElement.clientWidth) {
      elMenu.classList.add(classNames.leftward);
    }
    elMenu.classList.remove(classNames.loading);
  };
}

function attachStaticElements(dropdown: HTMLElement, focusable: HTMLElement, menu: HTMLElement) {

// * it delegates the module internal functions like `onLabelCreate` to the patched functions to add more features.
function ariaDropdownFn(this: any, ...args: Parameters<FomanticInitFunction>) {
  const ret = fomanticDropdownFn.apply(this, args);

  for (let el of this) {
    // dropdown will replace '<select class="ui dropdown"/>' to '<div class="ui dropdown"><select (hidden)></select><div class="menu">...</div></div>'
    // so we need to correctly find the closest '.ui.dropdown' element, it is the real fomantic dropdown module.
    el = el.closest('.ui.dropdown');
    if (!el[ariaPatchKey]) {
      // the elements don't belong to the dropdown "module" and won't be reset
      // so we only need to initialize them once.
      attachInitElements(el);
    }

    // if the `$().dropdown()` is called without arguments, or it has non-string (object) argument,
    // it means that such call will reset the dropdown "module" including internal settings,
    // then we need to re-delegate the callbacks.
    const $dropdown = $(el);
    const dropdownModule = $dropdown.data('module-dropdown');
    if (!dropdownModule.giteaDelegated) {
      dropdownModule.giteaDelegated = true;
      delegateDropdownModule($dropdown);
    }
  }
  return ret;
}
